To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the GE_LER retrieval is a new approach for the retrieval of GE_LER from UVN satellite data that is based on a physical model for GE_LER, the FP_ILM, and a retrieval method, the 1D-Var, that minimizes the differences between measured and modeled radiances.

the use of the FP_ILM for the retrieval of the GE_LER daily maps from the UVN measurements has the following advantages: (i) the GE_LER retrieval is based on the FP_ILM, which is a physically-based algorithm; (ii) the GE_LRE is retrieved for a large range of solar zenith angles (SZA) (i.e. 0-85 deg); (iii) the GE_LR is retrieved in the range of 0-90 deg;
The FP_ILM is able to retrieve the GE_LER with high accuracy, as demonstrated in a comparison with GE_LER derived from a 3-D model and with GE_LER from AERONET.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the retrieval of the effective reflectance of clouds and aerosols from satellite observations.
the retrieval of GE_LER from satellite measurements of reflected solar UV and visible radiation.
the retrieval of the Lambertian equivalent reflectance (LER) from the UVN (ultra violet and near infrared) satellite instruments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the retrieval of GE_LER maps from satellite measurements of UVN radiance is a challenging task.
the retrieval of the GE_LER is a very complex problem, which is not yet completely solved, and that it is not possible to provide a unique solution.

the retrieval of the effective Lambertian equivalent reflection (ELR) of the Earth's surface from satellite measurements of the Earth's reflected solar radiation is a difficult and complex problem, and the retrieval of the ELER of the Earth's atmosphere and clouds is a difficult and even more complex problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GE_LER retrieval is a very promising approach for the retrieval of aerosol optical properties from satellite measurements.

we developed a novel approach for the retrieval of GE_LER from the Ozone Monitoring Instrument (OMI) and the Global Ozone Monitoring Experiment-2 (GOME-2) instruments on board the Aura and MetOp satellites.

the use of FP_ILM in combination with the GE_LER retrieval algorithm allows us to retrieve daily maps of GE_LER at a spatial resolution of 0.25° x 0.25 ° and a temporal resolution of 1 day with high accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the cloud field is inhomogeneous, a single cloud optical thickness cannot represent the cloud radiative properties.
the retrieval of GE_LER from UVN measurements is a challenging task that can only be achieved with the use of a sophisticated retrieval scheme.
the use of the Lambertian equivalent reflectance (LER) concept is a good approximation of the actual reflectivity of the Earth's surface in the UVN region.
